knowledge:
- key_parameters: sequence=A DNAString object containing the nucleotide sequence to analyze ;; pfm=A PFMatrix object representing the binding preferences of a single transcription factor ;; pfms=A PFMatrixList object representing multiple transcription factors ;; cutoff=A numeric value between 0 and 1 (0 calculates total affinity by summing all subsequences; 1 sums only perfect matches; intermediate values represent trade-offs)
- alternatives: Classical single-site analysis (which uses a binary threshold to classify sites as binding or non-binding), which fails to capture low-affinity transient binding events.
- when_to_use: Use when you want to model transcription factor binding as a thermodynamic process, taking into account the cumulative effect of both high- and low-affinity sites across a whole sequence.
- pitfalls: Custom PFMs must contain integer count values and background frequencies ;; The perfect match sequence of a matrix can change depending on the background nucleotide distribution ;; A pseudocount of 1 is automatically added to zero counts in the PFM, which may slightly alter expected ratios.

workflows.name: tf_sequence_occupancy
workflows.intent: Calculate the total binding affinity or occupancy of single or multiple transcription factors on a target DNA sequence.
input: jaspar_db (JASPAR database or custom PFM counts)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the target DNA sequence into a DNAString object ;; 2. Retrieve or define the transcription factor PFMatrix or PFMatrixList ;; 3. Calculate the sequence occupancy or total affinity using getSeqOccupancy with a specified cutoff
workflows.code:
library(MatrixRider)
library(JASPAR2014)
library(TFBSTools)
library(Biostrings)
pfm <- getMatrixByID(JASPAR2014,"MA0004.1")
sequence <- DNAString("CACGTG")
getSeqOccupancy(sequence, pfm, 0.1)
getSeqOccupancy(sequence, pfm, 1)
pfm2 <- getMatrixByID(JASPAR2014,"MA0005.1")
pfms <- PFMatrixList(pfm, pfm2)
names(pfms) <- c(name(pfm), name(pfm2))
getSeqOccupancy(sequence, pfms, 0)
